name: 27-28 dominoes
description: 27-28 dominoes refers to block or draw domino games using a standard double-6 set of 28 tiles (0-0 through 6-6). Players draw 7 tiles each (4 players); highest double leads. Players match a number on an open end; doubles are placed crosswise. Cannot play: draw from boneyard or pass. First to empty hand wins and scores sum of opponents' pips; or lowest hand wins if blocked.

history.origins: Domino tiles were first recorded in Song-dynasty China, but modern double-6 domino sets and the 27–28 tile block/draw family emerged in 18th-century France and spread through Europe and North America.
timeline: Song-dynasty China (13th century): earliest recorded mention of domino tiles.
Mid-18th century France: modern double-6 dominoes and block/draw games spread through Europe and North America.

setup.dealing: Draw 7 each (4 players); remainder is boneyard.

rules.objective: Play all your tiles first, or have fewest pips if blocked.
rules.gameplay: Highest double leads. In turn, match one number to an open end. Doubles placed crosswise. If cannot play, draw until you can or boneyard empty then pass.
keyRules: Draw or pass if cannot play

strategy.basic: Get rid of high doubles and high tiles early.
strategy.advanced: Force block when you have few pips left; leave awkward ends for opponents.
tips: Play high doubles early to avoid getting stuck.
Block vs draw: agree before play.

scoring.description: Winner scores total pips in opponents' hands; or blocked game: lowest hand wins.
scoring.winCondition: Play all your tiles first, or have fewest pips if blocked.
